hormuz.headline: US and Israeli forces strike Iran; Iran retaliates and threatens to close the Strait of Hormuz to shipping.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard blocks routine commercial transits through Hormuz; major shipping lines suspend crossings.
US begins a naval blockade of Iranian ports as the conflict continues.
Over 1,500 vessels reported stranded near the strait, with more than 20,000 mariners affected.
A US-Iran memorandum of understanding reopens the strait toll-free, though traffic stays well below normal.
Attacks on commercial vessels resume; the strait is once again effectively closed to routine shipping.
Daily transits through the strait fall to roughly 10 vessels, against a pre-crisis baseline of 88-130 per day.
A tanker affiliated with UAE's state oil company ADNOC is attacked while transiting the strait; Iran is blamed.

red_sea.headline: Houthi forces resume attacks on Red Sea shipping as regional tensions escalate, reversing gains made since the October 2025 ceasefire.
A separate Houthi attack forces the closure of a strategic port in Yemen, adding to Red Sea route disruption.
